arxiv-2011-13659.title: Complete reducibility of subgroups of reductive algebraic groups over nonperfect fields IV: An F 4 F_{4} example
arxiv-2011-13659.creator: Falk Bannuscher, Alastair Litterick, Tomohiro Uchiyama
arxiv-2011-13659.description: Abstract Let k k be a nonperfect separably closed field. Let G G be a connected reductive algebraic group defined over k k . We study rationality problems for Serre’s notion of complete reducibility of subgroups of G G .

arxiv-2112-10898.title: Load-balanced Gather-scatter Patterns for Sparse Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2112-10898.creator: Fei Sun 1 , Minghai Qin 2 , Tianyun Zhang 3 , Xiaolong Ma 4 , Haoran Li 1 , Junwen Luo 1 , Zihao Zhao 5 , Yen-Kuang Chen 1 , Yuan Xie 1
arxiv-2112-10898.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fei Sun 1 , Minghai Qin 2 , Tianyun Zhang 3 , Xiaolong Ma 4 , Haoran Li 1 , Junwen Luo 1 , Zihao Zhao 5 , Yen-Kuang Chen 1 , Yuan Xie 1. Deep neural networks (DNNs) have been proven to be effective in solving many real-life problems, but its high computation cost prohibits those models from being deployed to edge devices.

arxiv-2305-01902.title: Flat beam plasma wakefield accelerator Thanks: This work was performed with support of the US Dept. of Energy, Division of High Energy Physics, under contract no. DE-SC0017648 and DESC0009914.
arxiv-2305-01902.creator: Pratik Manwani, Nathan Majernik, Joshua Mann, Havyn Ancelin, Yunbo Kang, Derek Chow, Gerard Andonian, James Rosenzweig
arxiv-2305-01902.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pratik Manwani, Nathan Majernik, Joshua Mann, Havyn Ancelin, Yunbo Kang, Derek Chow, Gerard Andonian, James Rosenzweig. Particle beams with highly asymmetric emittance ratios are expected at the interaction point of high energy colliders. These asymmetric beams can be used to drive high gradient wakefields in dielectrics and plasma. In the case of plasma, the high aspect ratio of the drive beam creates a transversely elliptical blowout cavity and the asymmetry in the ion column creates asymmetric focusing in the two transverse planes.

arxiv-2310-15282.title: Final velocity and radiated energy in numerical simulations of binary black holes
arxiv-2310-15282.creator: Emmanuel A. Tassone, Carlos N. Kozameh
arxiv-2310-15282.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Emmanuel A. Tassone, Carlos N. Kozameh. The evolution of global binary black holes variables such as energy or linear momentum are mainly obtained by applying numerical methods near coalescence,post-Newtonian expansions or a combination of both. In this paper, we use a fully relativistic formalism presented several years ago that only uses global variables defined at null infinity together with the gravitational radiation emitted by the source to obtain the time evolution of such variables for binary black holes (BBH) systems.

arxiv-2312-03892.title: A minimal model for the role of the reaction rate on the initiation and self-sustenance of curved detonations
arxiv-2312-03892.creator: Matei Ioan Petru Rădulescu, Aliou Sow Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Ottawa, Canada
arxiv-2312-03892.description: Abstract A minimal model for curved detonations is studied, illustrating the role of the reaction rate on the detonation speed and its propagation limits. The model is based on a simple extension of the minimal Fickett toy model for detonations based on the kinematic wave equation.

arxiv-2401-02452.title: The Compute Divide in Machine Learning: A Threat to Academic Contribution and Scrutiny?
arxiv-2401-02452.creator: Tamay Besiroglu, Sage Andrus Bergerson, Amelia Michael, Lennart Heim, Xueyun Luo, Neil Thompson
arxiv-2401-02452.description: Abstract There are pronounced differences in the extent to which industrial and academic AI labs use computing resources. We provide a data-driven survey of the role of the compute divide in shaping machine learning research. We show that a compute divide has coincided with a reduced representation of academic-only research teams in compute intensive research topics, especially foundation models.

arxiv-2406-06774.title: ComFeAT: Combination of Neural and Spectral Features for Improved Depression Detection
arxiv-2406-06774.creator: Orchid Chetia Phukan*, Sarthak Jain*, Shubham Singh*, Muskaan Singh, Arun Balaji Buduru, Rajesh Sharma
arxiv-2406-06774.description: Abstract In this work, we focus on the detection of depression through speech analysis. Previous research has widely explored features extracted from pre-trained models (PTMs) primarily trained for paralinguistic tasks. Although these features have led to sufficient advances in speech-based depression detection, their performance declines in real-world settings.

arxiv-2408-12908.title: Carrier Mobility of Strongly Anharmonic Materials from First Principles
arxiv-2408-12908.creator: Jingkai Quan, Christian Carbogno, Matthias Scheffler
arxiv-2408-12908.description: Abstract First-principle approaches for phonon-limited electronic transport are typically based on many-body perturbation theory and transport equations. With that, they rely on the validity of the quasi-particle picture for electrons and phonons, which is known to fail in strongly anharmonic systems.

arxiv-2410-22368.title: Project MPG: towards a generalized performance benchmark for LLM capabilities
arxiv-2410-22368.creator: Lucas Spangher Tianle Li William F. Arnold, Nick Masiewicki Xerxes Dotiwalla Rama Parusmathi Peter Grabowski, Eugene Ie Dan Gruhl
arxiv-2410-22368.description: Abstract There exists an extremely wide array of LLM benchmarking tasks, whereas oftentimes a single number is the most actionable for decision-making, especially by non-experts. No such aggregation schema exists that is not Elo-based, which could be costly or time-consuming.

arxiv-2510-09898.title: T2J : Learning Bug Context for PyTorch-to-JAX Translation with LLMs
arxiv-2510-09898.creator: Hung Phan, Son Le Vu, Ali Jannesari
arxiv-2510-09898.description: Abstract Despite recent progress of large language models (LLMs) on code translation among mainstream languages, translating PyTorch to JAX remains nontrivial. The two libraries, though both embedded in Python, differ in core design, execution semantics, and ecosystem maturity; JAX is newer and comparatively underrepresented in public code, and parallel PyTorch–JAX corpora are limited.

pmc-10632513.title: Delta radiomics analysis for prediction of intermediary- and high-risk factors for patients with locally advanced cervical cancer receiving neoadjuvant therapy
pmc-10632513.creator: Rong-Rong Wu, Yi-Min Zhou, Xing-Yun Xie, Jin-Yang Chen, Ke-Run Quan, Yu-Ting Wei, Xiao-Yi Xia, Wen-Juan Chen
pmc-10632513.description: This study aimed to assess the feasibility of using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based Delta radiomics characteristics extrapolated from the Ax LAVA + C series to identify intermediary- and high-risk factors in patients with cervical cancer undergoing surgery following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.

pmc-10736019.title: SEQUENCE ANALYSIS OF CARDIOMETABOLIC MULTIMORBIDITY AND ASSOCIATION WITH SUBSEQUENT DEMENTIA
pmc-10736019.creator: Corey Nagel, Heather Allore, Anda Botoseneanu, Jeffrey Kaye, Jason Newsom, Nicholas Bishop, Ana Quiñones
pmc-10736019.description: Sequence analysis is used in the social sciences to examine patterns of events occurring across the life course, but there are few examples of its use in multimorbidity research among older adults. We used sequence analysis to identify longitudinal patterns of cardiometabolic multimorbidity over a five-year period among participants in the National Health and Aging Trends Study (N=5,218).

pmc-11607075.title: Cellular internalization, cytotoxicity and DNA binding property of 2,3-diaminophenazine, synthesized using Jeanbandyite, a heterogeneous catalyst
pmc-11607075.creator: Subhadeep Sen, Subhankar Basak, Samit Pandit, Pappu Sarkar, Tae Wan Kim, Nandan Ghosh, Hye Jeong Kong, Jae Sung Ryu, Bhagat Singh, Rosni Roy, Rajib Mondal, Abhijit Saha, Seob Jeon, Sumantra Bhattacharya, Jungkyun Im, Goutam Biswas
pmc-11607075.description: In recent years, the development of novel chemistry routes for the synthesis of organic compounds has attracted special attention. 2,3-Diaminophenazine (DAP), a derivative of Phenazine, is a large group of nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound with diverse chemical structure and various biological activities, such as antibacterial, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. Phenazine is a fluorescent molecule with wide range of biological properties.

pmc-13213076.title: CGRP at the Neuroimmune Interface: Regulator of Host Defense, Tumor Immunity, and Tissue Homeostasis
pmc-13213076.creator: Cong Gao, Yue Shang, Xueyin Hu, Qianhui Wu, Longbo Ma, Bingwen Zou, Luntao Liu, Saijun Fan
pmc-13213076.description: Sensory neurons act as crucial hubs for host defense, tumor immunity, and tissue homeostasis by detecting environmental cues and fine-tuning immune responses. Across a diversity of tissues, these neurons establish specialized neuroimmune units with resident immune cells, translating local stimuli into coordinated physiological adaptations. Central to this crosstalk is calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP).

pmc-13301951.title: Life with Pain Revalued—A Therapist-Led Support Group for Patients with Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: A Pilot Feasibility Study
pmc-13301951.creator: Maciej Klimasiński, Piotr Krajewski, Daria Metelkina, Nicole Goldsztajn, Andrea Trondsdatter Haugland, Malwina Prus-Zielińska, Marcin Wnuk
pmc-13301951.description: Introduction. Chronic non-cancer pain is highly prevalent and profoundly diminishes quality of life. While pharmacological and interventional treatments are central, its psychosocial and spiritual dimensions remain under-addressed. This pilot study assessed the feasibility of a therapist-led support group intervention for patients with chronic non-cancer pain and explored preliminary psychospiritual outcomes. Methods.

pmc-13342129.title: The relationship between intimate partner violence and alexithymia in women of reproductive age and affecting variables: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13342129.creator: Fatma Başaran
pmc-13342129.description: AimStudies have shown that intimate partner violence has negative effects on women’s health. Understanding alexithymia and associated factors with depressive symptoms as a result of intimate partner violence may help develop screening strategies to identify at-risk women. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between intimate partner violence and alexithymia in women of reproductive age.
